text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe Haemophilia Association is demanding compensation from the government for some of its members who allegedly contracted the HIV virus through blood transfusions at a government hospital.

- President Robert Mugabe has been handed a report compiled by the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace and the Legal Resources Foundation on atrocities committed both by former freedom fighters and by security forces in the Matebeleland province in the 1980s.
- Prospective beneficiaries of the Z$780 million World Bank funding for small-scale enterprises have to put up 20 percent of the money they intend to borrow and no outstanding debts.
- Zimbabwe and South Africa on Thursday signed a bilateral agreement on road transport which should see both countries recognising each other's road service permits and other related documents.

- Management at state-owned Air Zimbabwe has appealed to its striking pilots and flight engineers to return to work immediately, promising to reach an amicable settlement over their grievances within two weeks of their resumption of duty.
